title: ShinColle-kai ship definition
description: One data/<namespace>/shincolle_kai/ships/<path>.json file, at most 65536 UTF-8 bytes and 32 nesting levels. ID comes only from the file path and must satisfy resourceLocation below. Duplicate JSON member names are rejected before validation. Unknown properties are warned about and ignored. Registry existence is checked by the server at reload; visual existence is deliberately deferred to the client placeholder mechanism.

display_name.description: Defaults to the file-derived namespaced ID.

dimensions.description: Dimensions must be at least the smallest positive IEEE 754 float (Float.MIN_VALUE) and remain positive when narrowed to float.

mount_offset.description: Riding height in blocks before scale-level scaling.

hostile_modifiers.description: Hostile ships use configured scale-tier values times these modifiers; they do not use base_stats or growth. Friendly ships ignore these modifiers. Values must be finite and at least the smallest positive IEEE 754 float (Float.MIN_VALUE), so narrowing to float cannot produce zero.

base_stats.description: Friendly ship base-table columns, not the 21 equipment attributes. Hostiles ignore these. Omitted columns are zero. Values must be finite. Bounds are twice the built-in column maxima; this does not change built-in ships.

growth.description: The corresponding six growth-table columns; omitted columns are zero. All values must be finite.

initial.description: Equipment definition IDs, not Item IDs. Must exist in the server equipment snapshot. Repetition is allowed in different slots. Count must not exceed slots.

ai.description: Defaults to shincolle_kai:standard when omitted. IDs outside the enum reject the whole definition; no unknown-ID fallback.

attacks.description: When omitted, friendly data-defined ships use shincolle_kai:light_cannon, shincolle_kai:heavy_cannon and shincolle_kai:melee; hostile data-defined ships use shincolle_kai:light_cannon and shincolle_kai:heavy_cannon. Selecting only one cannon excludes the other, even if its GUI setting is enabled. For friendly ships, melee works only while the admiral's melee setting is enabled; hostile ships use melee when explicitly selected. Empty arrays and IDs outside the enum reject the whole definition.

hostile_variants.description: Post-1.0 feature: this version only loads and validates this metadata. No selection, effects, recruitment transfer or rendering yet.

recruitment.description: Reserved, ignored regardless of its value in this version.

variants.description: IDs must be unique within a ship, even when other fields differ (checked by the server). Normal plus variant weights total at most 170000. All-zero weights mean a normal individual; rarity is display-only. This version does not perform the draw.

id.description: Stable ID, identified together with the ship ID; do not use array order or display names as identity.

hostile_modifiers.description: Same six keys and bounds as ship-level modifiers; separate from persistent traits. Metadata only in this version.

visual_variant.description: Individual texture ID, not geometry or animation. Existence is checked on the client.

shipAttackId.description: Selectable attack IDs. Reserved IDs shincolle_kai:aircraft, shincolle_kai:tenryuu_skill, shincolle_kai:tatsuta_skill and shincolle_kai:nagato_skill cannot be selected in this version and reject the whole definition.

acquisition.description: Normal hostile spawn weight. Built-in ships total 700; a built-in destroyer has weight 46. Bosses exclude data-defined ships.

construction.description: Construction is fixed when the shipyard completes. Material mode joins the material-dependent built-in pool; weight defaults to 100 (multiplier 1). Weighted mode uses weight/10000 regardless of materials; weight defaults to 0 and the total pool is proportionally capped at 50%. Disabled definitions never enter construction.

tier.description: Required for enabled material mode; omission in weighted mode allows both sizes.

material_bias.description: Subtract this material amount from the mean before computing distance; omitted means no bias.
